stats.fact: RUDR9 launched July 15, 2026 — reached 40 GitHub stars and 8 forks within 4 days
AgentsMesh leads the multi-agent orchestration space with 2,291 stars and 232 forks as of July 2026
Multi-agent coding tools saw explosive growth in 2026 — at least 8 distinct projects launched on HN in Q1-Q2 2026 alone
TeamFuse (Claude Code multi-agent template) has 14 stars since April 2026
Hermes Agent by Nous Research provides the underlying Kanban dispatcher with DAG dependencies, stale worker reclamation, and auto-blocking on failure
RUDR9 enforces 9 distinct roles with per-profile toolset restrictions — Planner physically cannot write code, Security Auditor physically cannot modify implementation

angles: RUDR9 is unique in building on top of an existing agent framework (Hermes) rather than being a standalone platform — lower barrier to entry for existing Hermes users
Hard authority enforcement via per-profile toolsets is a key differentiator — most competitors rely on prompt-based role separation
PAUL methodology (BDD acceptance criteria, STATE.md, SUMMARY.md) brings software engineering discipline to AI agent workflows
Scope-adaptive ceremony (quick-fix/standard/complex) addresses the cost-vs-quality tradeoff that other tools ignore
Ponytail philosophy (lazy senior developer) is a refreshing counterpoint to over-engineered agent orchestration
Sequential-by-default execution with opt-in parallelism is practical for solo developers — most competitors assume you want maximum parallelism
